title: Known issues: KV-cache evictions, rate-limit bursts, and private networking failures — mitigation playbook
author: Marcos Rivera
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook consolidates recurring customer-facing failures we see across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments in three clusters: (A) KV-cache evictions and stale-prefix hits, (B) sudden rate-limit bursts causing upstream 429s and tail latency, and (C) Private/VPC networking misconfigurations that manifest as TLS handshake or circuit errors during rollout. The goal is to provide triage steps, short-term mitigations, and owners for long-term fixes so CSRs and SREs can restore service quickly and communicate clearly to customers.

Impact and scope
----------------
- Affected services: redwood-hosted (api.redwood.ai), redwood-dedicated (customer-dedicated pools), redwood-private (VPC-controlled deployments).
- Typical customer symptoms: repeated 429s, responses truncated mid-stream, increased p95/p99 latency (>300ms), or model responses reverting to older pinned versions.
- Business impact: can cause failed user flows, increased error budgets for Dedicated accounts, and missed SLOs (default success SLO: 99.9% request success; latency SLOs: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for short-gen models).

Severity classification
-----------------------
1) Sev-1: complete outage for a customer or sustained 429s affecting >10% of requests over 10 minutes.
2) Sev-2: degraded throughput or intermittent 5xx/429 spikes (1–10% request error rate).
3) Sev-3: single-customer infrequent errors, increased latency but within error budget.

Reproduction checklist (quick)
------------------------------
1. Confirm customer environment: Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
2. Capture a sample failing request with headers (x-request-id, x-customer-id) and timestamps.
3. Verify model variant and version pin (route config).
4. Check cache keys and KV-cache metrics in Console -> Model -> Serving -> Cache (hit rate, eviction rate).
5. Query rate-limit counters for the API key: rctl metric request_count --key <API_KEY> --window 5m.
6. For Private: validate VPC peering / TGW logs and TLS cert rotation timestamps.

Common root causes and short-term mitigations
---------------------------------------------
A) KV-cache evictions and stale prefixes\- Symptoms: sudden drop in prefix hit-rate, repeated re-computation of KV keys, p95 token cost spikes.\- Short-term mitigations:
  - Increase per-model KV-cache retention on the route: set route.annotation.cache_ttl=600 (seconds) for 1–2 hours via Console or rctl: rctl route patch <ROUTE_ID> --set cache_ttl=600.
  - Temporarily reduce max-batch-size to reduce working-set: rctl route patch <ROUTE_ID> --set max_batch_tokens=1024.
  - If Dedicated, move traffic to a warm replica: Console -> Rollout -> Manual -> shift 30% to replica B.
\- Notes: these changes trade CPU/GPU compute for lower latency; communicate cost implications when escalating to Finance.

B) Rate-limit bursts and token throttling (429s)\- Symptoms: cluster of 429s with x-rate-limit-retry-after headers, sudden client retry storms.\- Short-term mitigations:
  - Implement soft-fallback: route policy to fallback model-variant (smaller or quantized): rctl route patch <ROUTE_ID> --set fallback_model=redwood/gpt-small-q4
  - Apply temporary per-key burst allowance: Support can add a 1-minute burst window via the console (owner: Billing/SRE approval required).
  - Enable exponential backoff recommendations in SDK: advise customer to use Redwood SDK retry policy with jitter (example snippet in Appendix).
\- Communication template (customer):
  - "We observed transient rate-limit bursts affecting X% of your requests between HH:MM and HH:MM. We applied a temporary fallback to a compatible variant and increased burst allowance while engineering completes a capacity fix. Expect metrics to stabilize within 10–15 minutes."

C) Private deployment networking / TLS issues\- Symptoms: TLS handshake failures, intermittent 502/524 from load balancer, or persistent connection resets after platform upgrades.\- Short-term mitigations:
  - Validate certs: ask customer to confirm cert rotation did not overlap (check cert expiry on control-plane and data-plane nodes: openssl s_client -connect <host>:443).
  - Restart local ingress (on-prem kube-proxy/ingress) in a rolling manner to avoid large reconnections: kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/ingress --grace-period=120.
  - If using customer-managed NAT, confirm ephemeral port exhaustion is not occurring; increase ephemeral port range temporarily.

Triage playbook (step-by-step)
------------------------------
1) Initial contact (CSR): collect request ID, route ID, customer environment, attach metrics snapshot (last 15m).
2) Triage call with SRE (if Sev-1/2): include owner on-call, CS engagement manager, and the customer's technical contact.
3) Apply short-term mitigations from A/B/C above relevant to the environment. Record any config changes in the customer incident log (Console -> Incidents -> Add note).
4) Restore traffic via canary or manual rollback if the issue is tied to a release. Use console rollout or rctl: rctl rollout rollback <ROLLOUT_ID>.
5) For Private: coordinate with customer for node-level logs (journalctl, kubelet logs) and share a secure log collection plan (s3 presigned or concierge collection by SRE).

Long-term fixes and owners
-------------------------
- KV-cache tuning: Eng-serving-runtime (owner: Priya Mehta) — objective: adaptive eviction policies and predictive prefetch (ETA Q3 2026).
- Rate-limit autoscaling: Eng-sre & Eng-platform (owner: Daniel Ortiz) — objective: burst-aware quota adjustments and per-api-key autoscaling (ETA Q2 2026).
- Private deployment networking hardening: Eng-private-deployments (owner: Laura Ng) — objective: improved health checks, TLS rotation orchestration, and a diagnostics agent (ETA Q4 2025).

Customer communication assets (copy/paste)
----------------------------------------
- Short incident update (first 30 minutes):
  "We are investigating elevated request failures. We've applied temporary mitigations and will provide an update within 30 minutes. Incident ID: INC-<yyyymmdd>-<nn>."

- Post-incident summary template (to be completed by CS + SRE):
  "Summary: root cause, timeline (first alert -> mitigations -> resolution), customer impact (requests affected, time window), remedial actions taken, and next steps (permanent fix ETA and owner)."

Runbook commands and diagnostic queries (examples)
--------------------------------------------------
- Fetch recent request traces for a customer (last 15m):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <SVC_BEARER>" 
    "https://console.redwood.ai/api/observability/traces?customer_id=<CID>&window=15m" 

- Check cache metrics (CLI):
  rctl metrics get cache_hit_rate --route <ROUTE_ID> --window 5m

- Apply temporary route TTL change:
  rctl route patch <ROUTE_ID> --set cache_ttl=600

- SDK retry policy example (NodeJS):
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, retry: { maxRetries: 5, baseDelayMs: 200, jitter: true } });

Config table (common knobs and guidance)
----------------------------------------
- cache_ttl: default 120s (increase to 600s for short-term to reduce recompute).
- max_batch_tokens: default 4096 (reduce to 1024 in memory pressure scenarios).
- per_key_burst_window: default 60s (support can raise to 120s for bursty onboarding at request).
- fallback_model: none by default (set to a compatible quantized variant when latency sensitive).

Post-incident checklist
-----------------------
1. Document the timeline and attach logs/traces.
2. Confirm permanent fix owner and target ETA.
3. Schedule a customer QBR follow-up if SLA was missed.
4. Update this known-issues page with final mitigations and new diagnostic queries.

Appendix: example customer-facing escalation timeline
----------------------------------------------------
- 00:00 – Alert received by CSR (collect metadata).
- 00:05 – Triage call with SRE and CS lead.
- 00:10 – Short-term mitigations applied (fallback + burst allowance).
- 00:25 – Metrics show stabilization; continue monitoring.
- 01:00 – Post-incident writeup draft sent to customer.

Glossary
--------
- KV-cache: per-route key-value cache used to store transformer KV caches for ongoing sessions.
- TTL: time-to-live for cached prefixes.
- P95/P99: 95th / 99th percentile latency.
